def workflow_stop(obj, names):
    """ Stop one or more running workflows.

    \b
    NAMES: The names, ids or job ids of the workflows that should be stopped.
           Leave empty to stop all running workflows.
    """
    if not names:
        names = [wf.id for wf in obj.workflows() if wf.is_running]

        raise click.ClickException('No workflows running.')

    obj.stop_workflows(names)

def workflow_start(obj, names, force):
    """ Start one or more stopped workflows.

    \b
    NAMES: The names, ids or job ids of the workflows that should be started.
           Leave empty to start all stopped workflows.
    """
    if not names:
        names = [wf.id for wf in obj.workflows() if wf.is_stopped]
    if not names:
        raise click.ClickException('No workflows stopped.')

    # Start workflows
    obj.start_workflows(names, force)


def workflow_delete(obj, names):
    """ Delete one or more workflows.

    \b
    NAMES: The names, ids or job ids of the workflows that should be deleted.
           Leave empty to delete all workflows.
    """
    if not names:
        names = [wf.id for wf in obj.workflows()]
    if not names:
        raise click.ClickException('No workflows available.')

    # Delete workflows
    obj.delete_workflows(names)


def workflow_show(obj, names):
    """ Show one or more workflows.

    \b
    NAMES: The names, ids or job ids of the workflows that should be shown.
           Leave empty to show all workflows.
    """
    if not names:
        names = [wf.id for wf in obj.workflows()]
    if not names:
        raise click.ClickException('No workflows available.')

    # Show workflows
    for wf in obj.workflows(names):
        click.echo(wf)
